events.title: The child Alfonso VII is crowned king of Galicia
events.description: The Galician high nobility, led by Pedro Fróilaz de Traba, crowned the child Alfonso VII king of Galicia at Santiago de Compostela, and Bishop Diego Gelmírez anointed him. The coronation was meant to preserve his rights in Galicia.

events.title: Seljuk forces ambush Manuel I Komnenos at Myriokephalon
events.description: The Seljuk sultan Kilij Arslan II ambushed the army of the Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos in a narrow pass as it marched on Konya. Manuel escaped and agreed a truce, but the defeat ended Byzantine hopes of recovering central Anatolia.

events.title: Louis the Great's daughter Mary is crowned ruler of Hungary
events.description: After Louis I of Hungary died without a male heir, his daughter Mary was crowned with the title of "King" of Hungary. She reigned until 1385 and again from 1386, while her sister Jadwiga succeeded Louis in Poland.

events.title: Charles VI orders the expulsion of the Jews from France
events.description: King Charles VI decreed that all Jews must leave the kingdom of France. The edict ended organised Jewish life in most of the kingdom for some four centuries.

events.title: Piotr Dunin's Polish army defeats the Teutonic Knights at Świecino
events.description: In the Thirteen Years' War, Polish forces under Piotr Dunin, some 2,000 mercenaries and Poles, decisively defeated the 2,700-man army of the Teutonic Knights under Fritz Raweneck and Kaspar Nostitz. Duke Eric II of Pomerania's auxiliaries stayed out of the battle.

events.title: Delegates sign the US Constitution in Philadelphia
events.description: Thirty-nine delegates signed the Constitution, creating a federal government with separated powers and checks and balances. The Bill of Rights was added by amendment in 1791.
events.html: Thirty-nine delegates signed the Constitution, creating a federal government with separated powers and checks and balances. The Bill of Rights was added by amendment in 1791.

events.title: The Battle of Antietam, America's bloodiest single day
events.description: Union and Confederate armies suffered about 23,000 casualties along Antietam Creek in Maryland. Lee's retreat gave Lincoln the victory he needed to announce the Emancipation Proclamation.

events.title: Operation Market Garden begins in the Netherlands
events.description: Some 35,000 Allied airborne troops landed to seize bridges leading to the Rhine. The operation failed at Arnhem, ending hopes of finishing the war by Christmas 1944.
events.html: Some 35,000 Allied airborne troops landed to seize bridges leading to the Rhine. The operation failed at Arnhem, ending hopes of finishing the war by Christmas 1944.

events.title: Egypt and Israel sign the Camp David Accords
events.description: After 13 days of talks hosted by Jimmy Carter, Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin signed two frameworks for peace. They led to the Egypt-Israel peace treaty of March 1979.
